provenance.notes: GUI worker, fresh boot per cell, selections by real pointer input except the script/command doors; numeric transforms applied as one scripted block while no tool session was live; drags by relative pointer increments; every cell journal passed the session gate with 0 in-session reads

index_map.note: cube vertices named as in our 8-vertex cube; captured indices differ for two of them

law.partner: a transform writes only the operand (the selection, or the whole mesh when nothing is selected); an unselected partner is never written -- by move, rotate, with or without a falloff
law.pairing_doors: pointer gestures pair (click, shift-click, ctrl-click deselect, region, double-click loop, in vertex/edge/polygon modes); script and command doors do not (the index selection command in set and add mode, the scripting API, expand); turning symmetry on does not widen an existing selection
law.authoring_side: each operand vertex on the AUTHORING side A takes the transform T; each operand vertex on the other side takes its mirror M T M. The side is a latched state: every press (on or off the handle) sets it to the press side, it survives a tool drop and re-arm, and a fresh session starts at -X (so a numeric apply with no earlier press authors on -X). A selected pair therefore stays mirror-symmetric; a lone vertex off A moves by the mirrored delta
law.weights: numeric door: falloff weights of a pair are read at its +X member (and a lone vertex uses its own position); the action centre handle sits on the +X member. Drag-door weights under a linear falloff are NOT measured (see notes)
law.on_plane: an on-plane vertex keeps its plane coordinate
law.authoring_side_latch: the side is latched wherever an action centre is placed: a tool ACTIVATION latches the handle's side (the handle sits at the +X half of the selection); every press latches the press side (move, rotate, edge extend alike, with symmetry on or off) only when the press PLACES the centre (a pinned selection centre is not moved by a press, and that press leaves the side at the centre's side); a selection change while a transform is armed re-activates it and so latches the re-centred handle's side; switching an action-centre tool on latches that centre's side (the origin gave -X). The side is global (one value across presets and tools), survives symmetry off/on and an axis change, and is not part of undo; undoing after a drop re-activates the tool, which re-latches
law.off_side_evaluation: an operand vertex off the authoring side is evaluated as M K(M p) with the whole transform K, pivot included; the one-block numeric door evaluates no action centre, so its pivot is the world origin

C-order.rig: 8-vertex cube +-0.5; one vertex (0.5,0.5,0.5) selected by a real click with symmetry OFF; symmetry X switched on; numeric move TX 0.4 (one scripted application)
C-order.verdict: O-sel: the selection is not widened when symmetry turns on and the unselected partner is never written

C-lone-neg.rig: symmetry X on; only (-0.5,0.5,0.5) selected by the scripting API (no selection command); numeric TX 0.4
C-lone-neg.verdict: not L-own as a law: the numeric value equals L-own only because the lone vertex lies on the side the numeric door authors on; with the press on the other side the same vertex takes the mirrored delta. Partner never written.

C-fall.rig: symmetry X; only (0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API); linear falloff start (-1,0,0) weight 1, end (1,0,0) weight 0, written after the arm and read back before the apply; numeric TY 0.4
C-fall.verdict: F-sel: the falloff does not widen the operand; the selected vertex moves by its own weight (0.25 * 0.4)

C-plane.rig: cube +-0.5 with 2 segments in X; symmetry X; real click on the on-plane vertex (0,0.5,0.5); numeric TX 0.4 TY 0.2
C-plane.verdict: P-proj: an on-plane vertex keeps x = 0

C-base.rig: symmetry X; pair selected; linear falloff giving weight 1 at x=-0.5 and 0 at x=+0.5 (C-base, C-base-td) or the reverse (C-base+); numeric TY 0.4; handle read after arming
C-base.handle_after_arm: drawn at the +X member (0.5,0.5,0.5) in all three cells (frame centre within 3 px of its projection), whichever side was clicked
C-base.verdict: B-fixed for the WEIGHT: a selected pair moves by the weight at its +X member, clicked side irrelevant; B-anchor and B-own refuted

C-script.rig: symmetry X; selection dropped before each door; index 6 = (0.5,0.5,0.5)
C-script.verdict: S-single on every script/command door: only a pointer gesture pairs

C-desel.rig: symmetry X; click (0.5,0.5,0.5); Shift-click (0.5,0.5,-0.5); Ctrl-click (-0.5,0.5,0.5); numeric TX 0.4
C-desel.verdict: D-pair: deselecting one vertex drops its partner too

C-lasso.rig: symmetry X; right-button region gesture whose closed outline encloses only (0.5,0.5,-0.5) (a triangle; see notes)
C-lasso.verdict: L-pair: the region gesture adds the partner of every enclosed vertex

C-edge.rig: edge mode; symmetry X; real click on the top edge at x = +0.5; numeric TX 0.4

C-poly.rig: polygon mode; symmetry X; real click on the +X face; numeric TX 0.4

C-loop.rig: cube +-0.5, 4 segments in X; edge mode; symmetry X; real double-click on the top edge at x = +0.25; numeric TX 0.4
C-loop.verdict: Lp-pair: the loop gesture selects the x = +0.25 loop AND the x = -0.25 loop (8 edges)

C-expand.rig: cube +-0.5, 4 segments in X; click (0.5,0.5,0.5) with symmetry OFF; symmetry X; select-expand command; numeric TX 0.4
C-expand.verdict: X-single: the expand command does not pair (4 vertices, all x > 0)

C-rot.rig: symmetry X; only (0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API); rotate 60 deg about Y around the ORIGIN, numeric
C-rot.verdict: Rp-stay: the unselected partner is not written by a rotation either; the lone +X vertex takes the MIRRORED rotation (numeric door); a pair rotates with the -X member taking the typed rotation and the +X member its mirror

C-elm.rig: no selection; symmetry X; element-move preset (range 0.044); press on a vertex and haul up 10 x 8 px
C-elm.verdict: Em-mirror: the picked vertex takes the drag and its partner the mirror, on either side

C-rot45.rig: symmetry X; only (0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API); rotate 45 deg about Y around the ORIGIN, numeric
C-rot45.verdict: Rt-conj: the lone +X vertex takes the conjugate rotation (RY -45 about the origin); the partner is untouched

C-mixed.rig: symmetry X; (0.5,0.5,0.5), (-0.5,0.5,0.5) and (0.5,0.5,-0.5) selected by the scripting API ((-0.5,0.5,-0.5) not selected); numeric TX 0.4
C-mixed.verdict: M-one-frame: the pair and the lone vertex follow ONE authoring side (-X on this door): pair members +-0.1, lone +X vertex 0.1, its partner untouched

C-unpaired.rig: symmetry OFF; (-0.5,0.5,0.5) moved to (-0.5,0.5,0.7) so (0.5,0.5,0.5) has no partner; select (0.5,0.5,0.5) by the scripting API; symmetry X; numeric TX 0.4
C-unpaired.verdict: U-reflect: the side rule applies with no partner at all

C-handle.rig: symmetry X; (0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API); move preset armed; press ON the handle centre (at that vertex, +X side) and haul 10 x 8 px right
C-handle.verdict: H-latch: a press on the handle also sets the authoring side to the press side (+X here): own delta

C-latch.rig: as C-handle but the press is OFF the handle at +X; haul right; tool dropped (Space); then a numeric TX 0.4 in a fresh arm
C-latch.verdict: P-persist: the side latched by the press survives the tool drop and re-arm; the numeric step moved the +X vertex by +0.4 (a fresh boot's numeric step moves it by -0.4)

C-rot-self.rig: symmetry X; only (0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API); rotate preset armed and activated (handle read: centred on the vertex), dropped; numeric RY 45 in one scripted block

pair_same_side_after_activation.note: (0.5,0.5,0.5)+(0.5,0.5,-0.5); handle at (0.5,0.5,0); activation latched +X so both are on the authoring side

pair_same_side_no_activation.note: same selection, numeric block only (authoring side -X)

mixed_sides_after_activation.note: (0.5,0.5,0.5), (0.5,0.5,-0.5), (-0.5,0.5,-0.5); handle at (0.5,0.5,0) = centroid of the +X half; authoring side +X

C-rot-self.verdict: Cj-affine: an operand vertex off the authoring side is evaluated as M K(M p) with the WHOLE transform K, pivot included (mixed cell: the -X vertex lands at M of its image's rotation about (0.5,0.5,0); Cj-linear would give (0.1464,0.5,-1.0607)). The self cell alone cannot show it: the activation latched +X, putting the vertex on the authoring side at its own pivot

C-scale-self.rig: as C-rot-self with the scale preset and numeric SX 2

two_segment_no_activation.note: same selection, numeric block only: pivot at the origin

C-scale-self.verdict: Cj-affine (mixed cell: the -X vertex to x -0.625 = 2p + c; Cj-linear -1.375)

numeric_door_pivot.rig: numeric transform applied in one scripted block, tool never activated
numeric_door_pivot.verdict: no action centre is evaluated on this door: every vertex pivots on the world origin (own side: RY45 about the origin; off side: the conjugate about the origin)

C-activation.rig: lone vertex selected; move preset armed and ACTIVATED (handle at the vertex), dropped with a key; numeric TX 0.4
C-activation.verdict: activation latches the authoring side to the handle's side (+X vertex: +0.4 own; -X vertex: +0.4 own)

C-latch-p.rig: (-0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API), so the activation latches -X; move preset; press OFF the handle at +X, haul 10 x 8 px right (the vertex takes the mirrored drag: the press latched +X); tool dropped with a key; numeric TX 0.4 through the combined T+R+S preset

control_fresh_combined_preset.note: fresh boot, (0.5,0.5,0.5), numeric TX 0.4 through the combined preset

C-latch-p.verdict: Lp-global: the side latched under one preset is used by another

C-latch-t.rig: (-0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API), so the activation latches -X; move preset; press OFF the handle at +X, haul 10 x 8 px right (the vertex takes the mirrored drag: the press latched +X); tool dropped with a key; symmetry off, symmetry X; numeric TX 0.4
C-latch-t.verdict: T-keep: toggling symmetry off and on keeps the side

C-latch-a.rig: (-0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API), so the activation latches -X; move preset; press OFF the handle at +X, haul 10 x 8 px right (the vertex takes the mirrored drag: the press latched +X); tool dropped with a key; symmetry axis Z, then X; numeric TX 0.4
C-latch-a.verdict: A-keep: an axis change and back keeps the side

C-latch-t-off.rig: symmetry OFF during the activation and the +X press (own drag); then symmetry X; numeric TX 0.4
C-latch-t-off.verdict: Toff-latch: a press made with symmetry off still latches

C-latch-u.rig: (-0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API), so the activation latches -X; move preset; press OFF the handle at +X, haul 10 x 8 px right (the vertex takes the mirrored drag: the press latched +X); tool dropped with a key; numeric TX 0.4 after an undo

undo_live.note: undo taken while the tool is still armed (no re-activation in the journal)

undo_after_drop.note: undo after the drop: the journal shows the undo re-activating the tool with its handle back at -X; the -X reading is consistent with that activation re-latching, so this door does not separate keep from revert

C-latch-u.verdict: U-keep: the side is not part of the undo history (live undo: -0.4). After a drop, undo re-activates the tool and the activation re-latches the handle's side, which here reads like U-revert

C-latch-x.rig: edge mode; the -X bottom edge selected (scripting API); edge-extend tool by its key; press OFF its handle at +X, haul right (offset +0.24 wrote the new edge at x -0.74: authored on +X); dropped; vertex mode; (-0.5,0.5,0.5) selected; numeric move TX 0.4
C-latch-x.verdict: X-shared: an extend press sets the same side the transform reads

C-latch-r.rig: (-0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API), activation -X; rotate preset; press OFF the ring at +X, haul 10 x 8 px right; tool dropped with a key; numeric TX 0.4 through the move preset

twin_press_neg_x.note: (0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (activation +X), rotate press off the ring at -X; numeric TX 0.4

void_first_readout.note: the first run read the side after a block that switched the origin action centre on, which re-latches -X (see C-latch-o); not scored

C-latch-r.verdict: R-latch: a rotate press latches the press side like a move press

C-latch-o.rig: (-0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API), so the activation latches -X; move preset; press OFF the handle at +X, haul 10 x 8 px right (the vertex takes the mirrored drag: the press latched +X); tool dropped with a key; one block: move preset + origin action centre switched on, TX 0.4
C-latch-o.verdict: placing an action centre re-latches the side: the origin centre gave -X (own +0.4)

C-latch-xp.rig: (-0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API), so the activation latches -X; move preset; press OFF the handle at +X, haul 10 x 8 px right (the vertex takes the mirrored drag: the press latched +X); tool dropped with a key; edge mode; +X bottom edge (scripting API); edge extend applied in one scripted block, offX 0.2, no press
C-latch-xp.status: dropped from the gate: a panel-typed offset before any press does not apply, and inside the tool every operation starts with a re-latching press; this scripted-block reading is kept as data only

C-press-pinned.rig: (-0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API); move preset armed and activated (handle at the vertex, -X) with the SELECTION action centre switched on in the same block; press OFF the handle at +X, haul 10 x 8 px right; the handle stays on the moved vertex (not at the press point); dropped with a key; numeric TX 0.4

twin_pipe_cleared.note: same, then Escape (clears the pipe: the selection centre reads off) and the vertex re-selected before the numeric step

control_relocating_centre.note: same rig without the selection centre: the handle jumps to the press point

C-press-pinned.verdict: P-acen: a press whose action centre is pinned does not latch the press side; the vertex follows the hand during the haul (own delta) and the side read afterwards is the pinned centre's (-X). With a relocating centre the same press latches +X

C-latch-sel.rig: (-0.5,0.5,0.5) selected (scripting API); move preset armed and activated (handle at the vertex, -X); while the tool is armed, a selection key: connected (all 8) or invert (the other 7); the handle re-centres on the +X half, (0.5,0,0); the journal shows a tool re-activation right after the selection command; dropped with a key; only (-0.5,0.5,0.5) re-selected (scripting API); numeric TX 0.4
C-latch-sel.verdict: S-latch: a selection change while a transform is armed re-activates the tool, and the activation latches the side of the re-centred handle (+X)

notes: Linear falloff with a DRAG cannot be driven here: the press re-fits the falloff to the symmetry-halved selection box (start = end), zeroing every weight; so the pair weight side on the drag door is open.

7146: the handle-press latch of 7145 (C-handle) is not separated from the activation latch: the activation had just latched the same side. Every other press cell pressed on the side opposite its activation.

7146: C-latch-u's committed-undo door and C-latch-r's first readout are confounded (re-activation; an action-centre switch in the readout block) and are kept only as notes; the live-undo twin and C-latch-r3 carry the verdicts.

7147: whether a press under a pinned centre re-latches the centre's side or latches nothing cannot be separated: every path to such a press has just activated the tool, which latched the same centre's side.
C-lasso's outline was a triangle enclosing one vertex; a closed rectangle path returning to its start selected nothing (kept as raw/C-lasso-r1-closedpath).
